outlook.statement: The Company anticipates a positive trend in performance indicators over the coming quarters and remains optimistic about achieving steady revenue growth, improved profit margins, and better return on capital employed (ROCE).

The domestic footwear industry remains well positioned for long-term growth, supported by rising formalization, evolving consumer preferences, increasing demand for branded and value-for-money products, and the recent GST rationalization on footwear up to ₹2,500 per pair. The Company remains focused on leveraging these opportunities through retail and digital expansion, product innovation and premiumization, stronger customer engagement, manufacturing efficiencies and disciplined cost management.

While near-term challenges may persist from input cost pressures, wage and employee benefit costs and fluctuations in consumer demand, the Company remains committed to improving productivity, optimizing its cost structure and strengthening margins while delivering quality products, enhanced customer experience and value for money to its consumers.

The Company remains committed to strengthening its CSR efforts and supporting initiatives that contribute to education, healthcare, sports, rural and community development, environmental sustainability, humanitarian assistance and the overall welfare of society.
The Company intends to progressively enhance the use of clean energy in line with operational requirements and commercial viability.

The Company is also evaluating emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced analytics, digital design and omni-channel solutions, wherever relevant, with the objective of improving operational efficiency, product development, customer experience and responsiveness to changing market requirements.

The outlook for the Indian footwear industry remains positive, supported by India's strong domestic consumption base, rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, premiumisation and increasing formalisation of the sector. The industry is expected to benefit from increasing adoption of branded footwear, growth in athletic and comfort categories, expansion of organised retail and rapid development of e-commerce and omnichannel distribution. Government initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing, improving quality standards and enhancing India's export competitiveness are expected to support the sector's medium- and long-term development. The Focus Product Scheme for the footwear and leather sector is particularly relevant to the industry's efforts to improve design capabilities, component manufacturing, machinery and productivity. The India-EU FTA also has the potential to create a meaningful new opportunity for Indian footwear exporters by improving access to one of the world's largest consumer markets.

The Company will continue to focus on product innovation, quality, brand strengthening, operational efficiency, omnichannel distribution and prudent cost management to participate in the long-term growth of the Indian footwear market.

The Company continues to focus on manufacturing productivity, product mix improvement, cost optimisation, inventory efficiency and working capital management to improve operating leverage and strengthen profitability.

Raw Material Risk: Volatility in prices of leather, synthetic materials, rubber, EVA, chemicals and other inputs may affect margins
Demand Risk: Changes in consumer sentiment, inflation and discretionary spending can affect demand, particularly in price-sensitive segments
Competition Risk: Increasing competition from organised domestic brands, international brands, private labels and digital-first players may exert pressure on market share and margins
Regulatory Risk: Changes in BIS standards, quality control requirements, environmental regulations, labour regulations and other statutory requirements may increase compliance costs
Foreign Exchange Risk: Changes in foreign exchange rates may affect the Company's export revenues, imported inputs and overall competitiveness
Trade Risk: Changes in tariff policies, FTAs, rules of origin and geopolitical developments may affect international trade
Inventory Risk: Rapid changes in fashion and consumer preferences can lead to shorter product life cycles and inventory obsolescence
Sustainability Risk: Increasing environmental expectations and regulatory requirements may require investment in sustainable materials and processes
Technology and Cyber Risk: Increasing dependence on digital commerce, technology and data systems exposes businesses to cybersecurity and technology-related risks
Credit risk on trade receivables
Liquidity risk
Market risk from foreign exchange rates and variable interest rates
Price risk on key raw materials (EVA, PU) due to crude oil price fluctuations
